question: Does posterior-risk pair acquisition beat a fixed factorial-hub pair design on a new randomly branching motif topology at matched total acquisition cost?
graph_rule: For motif j>0, choose one earlier motif child uniformly from indices 0..j-1 using an independent graph RNG seeded by system seed+81212; the other parent is a fresh root. The graph is a rooted random recursive tree. Coefficients use the existing independent RNG seeded by system seed+81211, preserving the coefficient law across topologies.
primary_endpoint: final noise-free feasible_motif_mse; lower is better
primary_gate: ratio of mean risk_pair error to mean factorial_hub_pair error below 0.80 and upper endpoint of two-sided 95% paired t interval for risk_pair minus factorial_hub_pair below zero
secondary_context: Report every arm, matched costs, per-system effect, and graph structure. Existing binary-tree and fanout outcomes are context, not pooled confirmation. No secondary contrast can override the primary gate.
interpretation: A pass supports an adaptive numerical pair-selection advantage on this one synthetic random-recursive graph family. It establishes neither broad topology generalization nor a foundation-model contribution. A failure leaves Track B unpromoted.
resource: CPU only, 40 independent systems, no GPU or closed-source model call. Archive all cells and receipts regardless of outcome.
forbidden: Do not alter graph rule, actions, learner, seeds, budget, endpoint, or threshold after inspecting study outcomes.
